title: Till The Stars Come Down (National Theatre) - review
transcript: hello and welcome to theater reviews with Paul S I'm here at the National Theater to see till the stars come down till the stars come down written by Beth steel is a shocking insight into the despair of post industrial Britain disguised as a hilarious comedy keep watching and I'll tell you more about what could turn out to be the best new play of 2024 but first please like comment and sub subscribe to this channel thank you at the heart of till the stars come down are three sisters we meet these delightful characters in the excitement of the morning when the youngest Sylvia is getting married you positively glow in the warmth of this ulent rockus occasion of bickering and bonding Hazel is played by Lucy black the eldest and the mother hen in the absence of their dead actual mother over overworked and over cheerful she is begrudging and bigoted Lisa mcgrillis plays Maggie glittery and wild but clearly unsettled CH Matthews as Sylvia is naturally nervous but the most forward-looking of the siblings they're joined by Auntie Carol she's a force of nature who deals with life in sarcastic Crips that are funny enough to have the audience in stitches her hard mouth shoots out words like a nail gun from opening line directed at Sylvia how are you doing sugar tits Lorraine ashburn's Larger than Life betrayal commands a stage in each of her scenes in the beginning all is light-hearted conversation and affectionate jibes the women's banter especially anti carols is full of outrageous metaphors and vulgar observations she talks of a woman who shaved pubic hair as a trail blazer with a razor an Unfaithful man would have shagged a frog if he could get it to hold still long enough Maggie liked the way a man looked at her making her feel like I was a potato in a famine and Hazel can't wear a fascinator because she's got a flat head we also meet Helen's children Leanne played by Ruby Stokes who's a teenager who wants to save the planet while being depressed by the possibility it is beyond saving Sarah is a confident little girl who dreams of being an astronaut it's an intimate setting that keeps us involved with Beth Steel's complex creations the audience is on all four sides looking at a stage floor almost filled with a revolve that when it turns enables us to get a fair view of all the characters props usually tables and chairs are taken on and off for the changing scenes somal Black's set enables director ban shani's deafly choreograph production to keep moving slickly this is a stereotypical workingclass Society of strong women and weak men be Steel's dialogue is so natural as they chat and interrupt and talk over one another and in her finest work to date she juggles many characters and situations the performances are so real that you almost feel you're members of the wedding party rather than an audience the ensemble cast are First Rate actors many of whom you'll recognize from the better quality TV dramas like Happy Valley and shart Hazel's husband John a shell of a man is given a mighty characterization by Derek riddle his rabbit-like eyes soft and nervous his body trembles with feeling Alan Williams plays Tony the Father of the Bride a stolid man of few words who oozes disappointment but who in a magical moment suddenly comes to life when he remembers winning a dazen competition in his youth his brother Pete played by Philip wit church is a Joker with weakness behind his twinkling eyes but for Leanne's mobile phone it could be 50 years ago in this East Midlands mining Community except the Minds have closed and Sylvia is marrying an enterprising Polish immigrant of whom there are quite a few in the area the team leaders are all Eastern European and look after their own says Hazel explaining why she failed to get a promotion you look forward to two and a half hours of Laugh Out Loud Comedy but it doesn't last the guests are celebrating Outdoors when a downpour sends them running for cover having warmed to these characters we now found ourselves going into a sometimes shocking journey of discovery about the truth of their lives the wedding's a chance for the Sisters to slip into the past when they were carefree and their beloved mother was still in their lives for a few hours Nostalgia fuel by drink brings out in some of them their true feelings and their desire to live a more fulfilling life onto the stage tumble unconsummated love unrealized ambition and a long-standing feud between the father and his brother the title appears to derive from wh Orton's poem death's Echo about our short meaningless lives and how we should dance while we can but existential talk in the play about the age of the universe and the destruction of humanity seems unnecessary in an already rich portrait of turmoil within a family the humor never quite stops but the play does become deeper and darker because this is a play about a community laid Low by the loss of the minds around which it prospered the once proud workingclass population now work in meaningless jobs in warehouses and supermarkets Hazel talks of lost men Lost Boys who once thought they'd have a better life it's a story that could be repeated in so many parts of post-industrial Britain parts that punish the country's Elite by voting for brexit you might think if the community has been crushed so have the dreams of the older characters of the sisters only the youngest Sylvia remains an optimist looking forward to married life and embracing change even if she does sometimes mystically wish that she could freeze her moments of Happiness the other two and Helen's husband John as well as the senior generation have seen their dreams crushed and they bemoan their unhappy disappointing lives by contrast the outsider the pole is positive about life Merck played by Mark won is willing to work hard at jobs as he calls them the kind that the others feel TR Captain to build a better life he exposes the sense of entitlement and the lack of ambition of the British natives like the pigs in the abattoir he once worked in they seem to know their fate he's also an outsider in this play an underdeveloped character and seemingly without any family or friends at the wedding now of course we're meant to be concentrating on the state of the British working class but it still feels like a clumsy piece of writing bigot trim among Sylvia's family kindled by their frustrations and lost power simmers and eventually boils over into a violent climax the empty shell of a community cracks and the sisterly bond is tested to the Limit I give till the stars come down four stars and all praise to the National Theater for presenting it some other theaters have all but abandon new writing in the face of funding Cuts but the national also operating on a reduced budget continues to nurture new writing like this superb play from Beth steel with its impressive large cast I hope you enjoyed this review or at least found it useful and if you did please like comment and best of all subscribe to this channel you'll be the first to know about my future reviews if you want to read them then go to theater. reviews and you can follow me on X masteran threads Instagram and Facebook thank you for watching
